Commentary of Ibn al-Jawzi (Zad al-Masir) on surah 67, verses 28–30:

His words, exalted is He: ﴿Say: Have you considered, if Allah destroys me﴾ with His punishment ﴿and those with me﴾ of the believers. Ibn Kathir, Nafi', Abu 'Amr, Ibn 'Amir, and Hafs from 'Asim recited "maʿiya" (مَعِيَ) with a fatha on the ya'. Abu Bakr from 'Asim and al-Kisa'i recited "maʿi" (مَعِي) with sukun. ﴿Or He has mercy upon us﴾ so that He does not punish us, ﴿then who will protect the disbelievers﴾, meaning, who will shield them and grant them safety ﴿from painful punishment﴾. The meaning of the verse is: We, with our faith, are between fear and hope. So who will protect you, with your disbelief, from the punishment? That is, because you have no hope like the hope of the believers. ﴿Say: He is the Most Merciful; we have believed in Him and upon Him we have relied﴾, whom we worship. "Fa-satalamūna" (فَسَتَعْلَمُونَ, "you will know"). al-Kisa'i recited "fa-sayaʿlamūna" (فَسَيَعْلَمُونَ, "they will know") with the ya', at the moment of witnessing the punishment, who is in clear error, we or you.

His words, exalted is He: ﴿If your water should become sunken﴾. We have explained this in [al-Kahf: 41] at "fa-man yatīkum bi-māʾin maʿīn" (فَمَن يَأْتِيكم بِماءٍ مَعِينٍ), meaning: with flowing water that the eyes can see and that buckets can reach.
